searchDocs.title: Installation​
searchDocs.content: Currently only available on pesde.

searchDocs.title: Details​
searchDocs.content: The goal of feces is not to directly handle your replication with remotes, but to provide the simplest, most efficient, and flexible way to replicate data between jecs worlds.  Feces requires a couple specific conditions to work correctly:  The components should all be created before a feces object is created.The components should all be the same entity ids, basically just create the replicated components in the same order on all worlds.

searchDocs.title: Client To Server
searchDocs.content: Client To Server warning This is not a recommended use of feces, but since one might want to minimize libraries used for replication or reduce manual replication logic in their own code, here is a fairly secure way to do it. Theoretically, you can follow two approaches: Each player will have their own entity for every component they can replicate to the server On the server, you would verify packets by making sure checking that the replicated entities contains the pair(replicated, replicated) component: --setting up an entity for a player to replicate to the server (on the server) world:set(entity, jecs.pair(replicated, replicated), sendingPlayer) --check packets local permission = world:get(entity, jecs.pair(replicated, replicated)) == sendingPlayer Or, on the client you will have to create replicated components under entities that the client knows it can replicate to the server On the server, you would have to filter() packets received from clients, and then check if the player who sent the packet has permission with: --setting up an entity for a player to replicate a specific component to the server (on the server) world:set(entity, pair(replicated, someComponent), sendingPlayer) --check packets local permission = world:get(entity, pair(replicated, someComponent)) == sendingPlayer Assuming you are using the simple setup, you can use the following code to replicate to the server: WIP

searchDocs.title: Simple​
searchDocs.content: This option reduces code written and tools needed. In most cases, developers don't need to implement anything more complex than this unless they will be using feces to replicate large amounts of data often.  if RunService:IsServer() then requestFullPacket.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player) remote:FireClient(player, feces.full()) end) else requestFullpacket:FireServer() remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(data) feces.apply(data) end) end local function replicate() local changes, deleted = delta() if not next(changes) and not next(deleted) then return end for player, packet in feces.combine(changes, deleted) do remote:FireClient(player, packet) end end

searchDocs.title: Advanced Setup
searchDocs.content: Advanced Setup This example will use Blink to show how you could optimize packet size. The same concepts can likely be applied to any other serialized networking library. In our blink file events like requestFullPacket and entityDeleted are -- network.blink event requestFullPacket { from: Client, type: Reliable, call: SingleAsync } type Entity = u16 event entityDeleted { from: Server, type: Reliable, call: SingleAsync, data: u16[] } map EntityMap<T> = { [Entity]: T } enum SpecialChange = { __n, __d } struct ComponentPacket<T> { value: EntityMap<T>, special: EntityMap<SpecialChange> } event component { from: Server, type: Reliable, call: SingleAsync, data: (Entity, ComponentPacket<unknown>) } event componentTransform { from: Server, type: Reliable, call: SingleAsync, data: ComponentPacket<CFrame> } -- ... You'd have to make a new event to properly optimize replicating each component This is very close to actual code we use at killergg for optimally replicating commonly used components. It might be verbose, but it gets the job done. local function fire(network, player, component, entities) local remote = network[`component{getNameFromComponent(component)}`] if remote == nil then network.component.fire(player, component, entities) return end remote.fire(player, entities) end local function replicate() local network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Blink.Server) local fullPacket = nil for _, player in network.requestFullPacket.iter() do fullPacket = fullPacket or full() for component, data in fullPacket do fire(network, player, component, data) end end local changes, deleted = delta() for component, players in changes do for player, entities in players do fire(network, player, component, entities) end end for player, entities: { number } in deleted do network.entityDeleted.fire(player, entities) end end local function receive() local network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Blink.Client) for _, component, entities in network.component.iter() do apply({ [component] = entities }) end for name, id in Components do local remote = network[`component{getNameFromComponent(name)}`] if not remote then continue end for _, entities in remote.iter() do apply({ [id] = entities }) end end for _, entities in network.entityDeleted.iter() do apply({ __d = entities }) end end

searchDocs.title: Group​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Group { origin: string-- Human-readable origin for warnings and debugging (e.g. "script:23 reserve()") size: number-- Maximum count of entities for this group lookups: {[LocalEntity]: LookupEntity}-- Mapping local entity -> lookup id refs: {[LookupEntity]: LocalEntity}-- Mapping lookup id -> local entity } An object representing a reserved or default lookup namespace. The feces instance itself behaves as a Group when used as the default/global group.

searchDocs.title: Applyable​
searchDocs.content: </> type Applyable = { [Component]: {[LookupEntity]: { value: any, action?: number, }}, __d={LookupEntity} } Represents a per-player packet that can be applied locally. Use feces:apply to enact the changes in Applyable into the feces.world.

searchDocs.title: Changes​
searchDocs.content: </> type Changes = {[Component]: {[Player ]: { value: {[LookupEntity]: any}, remove: {LookupEntity}, none: {LookupEntity}, }}} Produced by feces:delta and accepted by feces.combine.

searchDocs.title: Deletes​
searchDocs.content: </> type Deletes = {[Player ]: {LookupEntity}} Produced by feces:delta

searchDocs.title: LocalEntity​
searchDocs.content: </> type LocalEntity = number An entity in the world at feces.world

searchDocs.title: LookupEntity​
searchDocs.content: </> type LookupEntity = number An lookup id for an entity that may exist in feces.world.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> lib.new( jecs: Jecs,-- The jecs module instance (require("@rbx/jecs")). world: World,-- The jecs.World instance to observe and mutate. group?: Group,-- Optional initial group to use for the returned instance (creates default group). debugPrints?: boolean-- Enable debug printing. ) → feces-- Returns a new feces instance. Creates a feces library instance that watches the supplied world for component changes and exposes apply, delta, full, reserve, and other helpers. -- may be used like this in a module of its own local world = jecs.world() local feces = lib.new(jecs, world)

searchDocs.title: combine​
searchDocs.content: </> lib.combine( changes: Changes,-- The changes object returned from delta. deleted: Deletes?-- Optional deletes object returned from delta. ) → {[Player ]: Applyable}-- Per-player packets prepared from the changes+deletes. combine translates Changes objects into per-player Applyable packets, ready to be serialized or sent to each client as one object with all the necessary updates. See the simple setup here.

searchDocs.title: reserve​
searchDocs.content: </> lib.reserve( size: number,-- number of lookup slots to reserve debugLocation: boolean?-- whether to use debug.info for debugging ) → Group-- A Group object with its own lookup space. Reserves a lookup namespace of size entries and returns a Group. The returned Group can be passed to lookup, ref, delta, apply, etc., to isolate replication to that namespace. Use feces:setGroup to add a particular entity to a replication group. The primary goal of these is to allow serializing entites of specific types with a set amount of bits. So for example, you could have a maximum of 8 racecars at a time in your racing game, and you could create a replication group with a size of 8, and then serialize those entities' lookup ids as 3 whole bits. Or if you're feeling fancy you can reserve a group then create an instance of feces from it: local group = lib.reserve(24) lib.new(jecs, myWorld, group)

searchDocs.title: added()​
searchDocs.content: Hooks onto when a new entity is replicated to the world, not for new components. The added callback is called after all the components received are set to a newly replicated entity. This is because there has to be at least one replicating component under an entity for it to be added through feces.  feces.added(function(entity) if world:has(entity, PlayerTag) then print("new player added", entity) return end print("entity added", entity) end)

searchDocs.title: changed()​
searchDocs.content: Hooks onto when a component value is changed in the world. Called before the component's new value is set in the world. This means that you can get whether the entity has the component or not, and the previous value of the component.  This also allows you to check for values being set to nil and compare previous and current values.  feces.changed(function(entity, component, value) local had = world:has(entity, component) if not had then print("component added", component) return end local previous = world:get(entity, component) print("component changed", component, previous, "->", value) end)

searchDocs.title: removed()​
searchDocs.content: Hooks onto when a component is removed from the world. Called before removing the component from the world. This means that you can get the previous value of the component.  feces.removed(function(entity, component) local previous = world:get(entity, component) print("component removed", component, "had the value of", previous) end)

searchDocs.title: deleted()​
searchDocs.content: Hooks onto when an entity is deleted in the world. This is called before the entity is deleted, allowing you to get the component values and clean up, fairly straightforward.  feces.deleted(function(entity) if world:has(entity, PlayerTag) then print("player has left the game", entity) return end print("entity deleted", entity) end)

searchDocs.title: _debug​
searchDocs.content: </> feces._debug: boolean? When true, the library prints debug traces using feces:debug. This is intended to be set by new but I guess you can enable/disable whenever you want to debug specific code.

searchDocs.title: jecs​
searchDocs.content: </> feces.jecs: jecs The jecs module instance used by this library.

searchDocs.title: world​
searchDocs.content: </> feces.world: World The jecs.World instance this feces object observes and mutates.

searchDocs.title: replicated​
searchDocs.content: </> feces.replicated: Entity The replicated component id used to indicate per-entity player routing.

searchDocs.title: refs​
searchDocs.content: </> feces.refs: {[number]: number} Lookup table: lookupId -> localEntity for this group.

searchDocs.title: lookups​
searchDocs.content: </> feces.lookups: {[number]: number} Reverse lookup: localEntity -> lookupId for this group.

searchDocs.title: ref​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:ref( key: LookupEntity?, group: Group? ) → LocalEntity Find a local entity from a lookup id in group. Allocates a local entity if needed. Use feces.refs or group.refs if you simply want to check for a local entity.

searchDocs.title: lookup​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:lookup( entity: LocalEntity?, group: Group? ) → LookupEntity Resolve/allocate a lookup id and entity (if needed) in group. Find a lookup id for a local entity in group. Allocates a local entity if needed. Use feces.lookups or group.lookups if you simply want to check for a lookup id.

searchDocs.title: added​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:added(callback: (LocalEntity) → ()) → () Register an "added" hook called when new local entities are created by incoming packets.

searchDocs.title: changed<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:changed<T>(callback: ( LocalEntity, Component, T ) → ()) → () Register a "changed" hook called when a component value is set.

searchDocs.title: removed​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:removed(callback: ( LocalEntity, Component ) → ()) → () Register a "removed" hook for removals.

searchDocs.title: deleted​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:deleted(callback: (LocalEntity) → ()) → () Register a "deleted" hook for entity deletions.

searchDocs.title: setGroup​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:setGroup( group: Group?,-- The group to assign (nil means default group) entity: LocalEntity-- The local entity to move ) → () Assigns entity to group (or to the instance default group). Useful when you need to move an entity between replication namespaces. The implementation will update refs/lookups.

searchDocs.title: getGroup​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:getGroup(entity: LocalEntity) → Group Return the Group currently owning entity. If the entity is not assigned to a non-default group the result is the feces instance (default group).

searchDocs.title: delta​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:delta(group: Group?) → ( Changes, Deletes ) Compute the pending changes and deletes for the provided group (or default). delta consumes internal buffers used to collect component changes; repeated calls without new changes return empty results. The result can be passed to combine for simple unified replication data.

searchDocs.title: full​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:full(group: Group?) → Applyable Produce a full replication packet for group (or default). This enumerates all currently replicated components and packages them into an Applyable suitable for sending to a player that needs the full current state for the group.

searchDocs.title: apply​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:apply( delta: Applyable,-- Packet to apply to the world. group: Group?-- Apply using the group's lookup mapping; defaults to the instance group. ) → () Apply a replication packet to the local world. apply will create entities for lookup ids, call hooks (added, changed, removed, deleted) as appropriate, and perform jecs mutations.

searchDocs.title: debug​
searchDocs.content: </> feces:debug(...: any) → () Internal debug function that prints only when feces._debug is truthy.
